papers.title: M\"obius-Pseudorandomness for Algebraic Circuits
papers.abstract: We define a notion of M\"obius-pseudorandomness for integer sequences generated by multivariate polynomials computed by small and simple algebraic circuits. This mirrors a related definition of Kalai that concerns boolean functions computed by small boolean circuits. We then prove M\"obius-pseudorandomness results for polynomials computed by algebraic circuits with few multiplication gates (of any depth), for polynomials with small-dimensional partial derivative space, and for the determinant and permanent. We conjecture that these results hold in general for polynomial-size algebraic circuits.

papers.title: Up or down at every integer: Collatz-type maps of arbitrary sets and the up-down graph
papers.abstract: For a set $S$ of positive integers let $T_S$ send $x$ to $\lceil 3x/2\rceil$ if $x\in S$ and to $\lceil x/2\rceil$ otherwise. The odd numbers give the Collatz map, the even numbers give it again after a shift by one, and $S=\mathbb{N}$ gives Mahler's map $x\mapsto\lceil 3x/2\rceil$. All these maps are subgraphs of the up-down graph $G$, in which every $x$ has the edges $x\to\lceil x/2\rceil$ and $x\to\lceil 3x/2\rceil$, and so are the families of maps in which the direction is forced at some numbers and free at the others. The cycles of the maps are the simple cycles of the subgraph, their divergent orbits are its rays, and all maps of a family are bounded exactly when the subgraph has no ray. We classify the simplest sets and show that density says little: some sets of density one send every orbit to 1, and some periodic sets of arbitrarily small density have increasing orbits. Every positive integer is the least element of a cycle of some map. The critical proportion of steps up is $\log_3 2$: cycles stay below it, divergent orbits stay above it, and both come arbitrarily close. For sets periodic modulo a power of 2, an effective up-frequency from a finite Markov chain takes the place of the density, and a finite computation can prove that every orbit reaches a cycle. Mahler's Z-number problem is implied by a question about one such map. Finally, we ask how far the Collatz map is from maps whose behaviour can be proved. Finite changes never help. Adding fewer than $\log_{3/2}N+1$ even numbers below $N$ makes an orbit increase, while removing the odd numbers congruent to 9 or 15 modulo 16, an eighth of all integers, gives a map all of whose orbits provably reach the cycle (1,2); removing 22 residue classes modulo 512, a proportion 0.043, also suffices.

papers.title: On the boomerang spectrum of the APN power function $x^{q+2}$ over $\F_{q^2}$
papers.abstract: We study the boomerang spectrum of the almost perfect nonlinear power function $x^{q+2}$ over $\F_{q^2}$, where $q$ is an odd prime power with $q\equiv1\pmod6$. The connection of Pal and St\u{a}nic\u{a} between boomerang entries and $(-1)$-differential entries reduces the problem to counting roots of a single equation. We determine the complete contribution from nonzero parameters in $\F_q$. For parameters outside $\F_q$, we obtain a quintic over $\F_q$ in terms of the parameter's trace and norm, with a separate formula when the trace is zero. We exclude the entry four when $q\equiv1\pmod{12}$ and characterize its occurrence when $q\equiv7\pmod{12}$ through a repeated-root parametrization and a residual cubic. We also evaluate the first nonsubfield moment and an aggregate quadratic-character sum, and prove a Weil bound for each nonzero trace. Explicit secant and residual-cubic formulas express the second, third, and fourth falling-factorial moments as finite sums. Once the size-four frequency is known, these moments recover all remaining frequencies through a nonsingular five-dimensional system. A closed-form evaluation of the nonsubfield distribution remains open.

papers.title: Gaussian mass inequalities for lattices
papers.abstract: The Gaussian mass of a lattice is the evaluation of its theta series at a real nome and is relevant to lattice coding for the wiretap Gaussian channel. The ratio of the Gaussian mass of stable lattices to the Gaussian mass of the integer lattice was conjectured to be $\le 1$ (Regev et al., 2024). Kominers proved this bound recently for lattices obtained by Construction~A from binary self-dual codes. Building on Kominers' bound, we establish corresponding inequalities on average for Construction~$A_4$ lattices obtained from free self-dual quaternary codes and for Construction~$A_6$ lattices obtained from self-dual senary codes. We also prove the strict Gaussian-mass inequality for extremal unimodular lattices of both Type~II and Type~I. The Type~I result uses the Rains--Sloane definition of extremality. Its proof combines a universal theta truncation with an exact inversion of the shadow coefficients, and a Gaussian inequality for translated lattices. In addition, we obtain an averaging bound over the genus of Type~II lattices, and extend the binary Construction~A inequality to Siegel theta series of arbitrary genus, with further quaternary results under conditions on the residue code.

papers.title: Equivariant homomorphisms and Mordell--Weil groups of twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes
papers.abstract: Let $X'\to X$ be a Galois cover of smooth projective varieties over a field $k$ with group $G$, and let $G$ act on an abelian variety $A$ over $k$. We prove an exact sequence relating the Mordell--Weil group of the twist of $A$ by $k(X')/k(X)$ to the group of $G$-equivariant homomorphisms from the Albanese variety of $X'$ to $A$; the remaining obstruction is killed by $|G|$. This corrects structure theorems in two earlier papers of the author and in a corrigendum to the first, where the equivariance condition was omitted. For the twists of Albanese varieties of cyclic multiple planes considered in those papers, we determine the rank and the torsion subgroup. Over number fields we describe the rank through the Galois action on endomorphisms and prove a specialization result. When $F(x,y)=0$ is the dual of the Fermat cubic, the Mordell curves $y^2=x^3+16F(a,b)$ have rank at least $3$ over $\mathbb Q$ for all $(a,b)\in {\mathbb Q}^2$ outside a thin set.

papers.title: On Minima of 3D Lennard-Jones Lattice Energy and FCC-Tetragonal-Simple Hexagonal Phase Transitions
papers.abstract: Denote the Epstein zeta function by \begin{equation}\label{eq:Epstein} E(L,s):=\sum_{v\in L\setminus\{0\}}|v|^{-2s}, \;\;\hbox{where}\;\;L\;\;\hbox{is a lattice}; \qquad s>\frac32. \end{equation} We consider the three-dimensional Lennard--Jones lattice energy, which has the form \[ \mathcal E(L)=\frac12E(L,6)-E(L,3). \] We completely classify the minimizers at every covolume $|L|$, and we prove that as the covolume increases, the minimizing phase changes from the FCC to the body-centered tetragonal and then to the simple-hexagonal lattice. Thereby, we give a positive answer to an open problem raised by Blanc--Lewin [EMS Survey Series 2015, Section~2.5,~(27), pp.~268--269] and B\'etermin--Petrache [JMP 2017, Question~1.15], and we prove and clarify the conjecture of B\'etermin--\v{S}amaj--Trav\v{e}nec [SAM 2023].

papers.title: The unitary group $U_3(4)$ as a Galois group over $\mathbb{Q}$
papers.abstract: We prove that the simple unitary group $U_3(4)=\operatorname{PSU}_3(\mathbb{F}_4)$, of order $62400$, is the Galois group of a regular extension of $\mathbb{Q}(t)$, and hence of infinitely many extensions of $\mathbb{Q}$. The extension has four branch points, with inertia groups of orders $2$, $2$, $3$, $3$, and it is the only extension with these properties up to a rational change of the coordinate $t$. We give an explicit polynomial of degree $65$ for it.

papers.title: N\'eron Functions on Jacobians of Odd-Degree Hyperelliptic Curves
papers.abstract: We express N\'eron functions on Jacobians of odd-degree hyperelliptic curves of arbitrary genus in terms of admissible pairings, using the pullback of the theta divisor via a generalized Abel--Jacobi morphism. Over non-archimedean local fields, we relate N\'eron functions to local N\'eron pairings on the curve and, moreover, deduce a comparison between unramified $p$-adic N\'eron functions and unramified local Coleman--Gross height functions. Furthermore, we decompose the N\'eron function into an intersection term $I$ and a Green function term $T$, and compute $T$ for specific semistable reduction types. We compare our decomposition with other decompositions in the literature.

papers.title: A geometric approach to the uniform boundedness of $\ell$-primary torsion points
papers.abstract: We prove that for a non-isotrivial abelian scheme over a smooth curve, the genus of a generic sequence of multi-sections with small heights tends to infinity. As an application, we give a new proof of the uniform boundedness of $\ell$-primary torsion points on fibers of an abelian scheme over a smooth curve, a result originally proved by Cadoret and Tamagawa. Furthermore, our approach allows us to reprove a conjecture of Cadoret and Tamagawa without additional assumptions. Our approach is based on the theory of Betti foliations and the arithmetic equidistribution theorem.

papers.title: An analogue of irreducible cuspidal representations for the group $PGL(2)$ over a two-dimensional local field
papers.abstract: Let $F$ be a local non-archimedian field of odd residue characteristic and let $G=PGL(2)$. In this paper we study an analog of irreducible cuspidal representations of the group $G(F)$ when $F$ is replaced by the field $K=F((t))$. The story turns out to be similar to the classical case, but also with some differences. We present a construction of such representations essentially (up to a small subtlety) starting from a quadratic extension $L$ of $K$ and a character $\theta:L^*/K^*\to \mathbb C^*$ which is not Galois invariant. We also show that the restriction of the representations we construct to the group $P(K)$ (here $P$ is a Borel subgroup of $PGL(2)$) is irreducible. However, contrary to the classical case it turns out that these restrictions are not isomorphic to the "standard" irreducible cuspidal representation of $P(K)$. In the Appendix we propose a notion of cuspidality for smooth representations of the group $H(K)$ for an arbitrary split reductive group $H$.

papers.title: On The Manin Constant
papers.abstract: We prove the Manin constant conjecture for every optimal elliptic curve over $\mathbb{Q}$ and Stevens' Conjectures I and II. Our method adapts Hongbo Yin's congruence argument for cubic roots of modular functions to lifts of modular parametrizations through isogenies, using the unbounded denominators theorem of Calegari, Dimitrov and Tang.

papers.title: On the Characterization Problem for Krull Monoids with Homocyclic Class Group
papers.abstract: This paper addresses a central problem in the factorization theory of Krull domains in which every class contains a prime divisor. It is well-known that the system of length sets depends on the class group only and the question is whether this system carries enough information to recover the underlying class group. We give an affirmative answer for all homocyclic class groups $C_n^r$. More precisely, let $D$ be a Krull domain with class group $C_n^r$, with $n, r \in \mathbb N$, and suppose that each class contains a prime divisor. If the system of length sets $\mathcal L (C_n^r)$ is equal to a system of length sets $\mathcal L (G)$, for any finite abelian group $G$ with $\mathsf D (G) \ge 4$, then $G \cong C_n^r$. The central tools are cross numbers of (minimal) zero-sum sequences over the class group.

papers.title: Computing extensions of flag-jump t-modules
papers.abstract: We study Anderson t-modules whose positive-degree coefficient matrices admit a flag-jump basis and extend the t-reduction algorithm to this setting. We prove that these t-modules are abelian, with motive rank equal to the sum of their jump degrees. If $\Phi$ has jump degrees $j_1,\ldots,j_d$ and $deg_\tau\Psi<\min_s j_s$, we compute the t-module structure on ${\mathbf{Ext}}^1_\tau(\Phi,\Psi)$, its subgroup ${\mathbf{Ext}}_{0,\tau}(\Phi,\Psi)$, and the associated exact sequence. The construction allows nonzero nilpotent constant terms and includes the strictly pure case. When $\Psi$ is the Carlitz module, $N_\Phi=0$, and all jump degrees are at least two, the construction yields a dual t-module. We give complexity bounds for the algorithms and implementations in SymPy and Mathematica.

papers.title: An asymptotic resolution of the Gao--Thangadurai conjecture on the Harborth constant
papers.abstract: The Harborth constant $\mathsf g(G)$ of a finite abelian group $G$ of exponent $n$ is the least integer $k$ such that every subset of $G$ of size at least $k$ contains $n$ elements whose sum is zero. Let $C_n$ be a cyclic group of order $n$. Gao and Thangadurai \cite{gt} in 2004 conjectured that $\mathsf g(C_n\oplus C_n)=2n+(-1)^n$ for all integers $n\ge3$. We prove this conjecture for all sufficiently large integers $n$.

papers.title: A New Record for the Katz-Tao Sum-Difference Exponent
papers.abstract: We prove the record bound $C_{3b}\le 209357544569848128/114631769327023765=1.8263483657186\ldots$ for the Katz-Tao sum-difference exponent, valid in every abelian group without $2$-torsion. Using only Shannon inequalities, conditional copies and Katz-Tao's original directions, whose classical single-grid argument gives $11/6$, we break $11/6$, obtaining $2762/1509$ and $152/83$. For every abelian group we prove the universal bound $C_{\mathrm{all}}=10304335425987192362/5641833174538280329=1.8264161855212\ldots$, which is below the previous record for the real Katz-Tao constant. In the AlphaEvolve study (arXiv:2511.02864v3), the search for extremal distributions improved this constant's lower bound in the eighth decimal place and left its upper bound at $11/6$. Our upper bounds are proofs discovered by CASPAC, the computational mathematics engine of the CASP research system, and certified by independent exact checkers. The proofs use stacked entropy certificates; we supply the complete rational identities, proofs of every auxiliary inequality, and exact verification over the stated group classes.

papers.title: A Proof of Stein's Equidissection Conjecture
papers.abstract: In 1970 Monsky showed that a square cannot be dissected into an odd number of equal-area triangles. His proof used an ingenious colouring of the plane based on a 2-adic valuation on $\mathbb{R}$ together with Sperner's lemma. Subsequent work established similar results for regular polygons, centrally symmetric polygons, and polyominoes. In 2000, Stein proposed a common generalisation of the centrally symmetric and polyomino cases to balanced polygons. In 2014, Rudenko introduced a new perspective on the problem and proved Stein's conjecture for dissections with rational vertex coordinates. Building on and streamlining his approach, we resolve the conjecture in full.

papers.title: Local limit theorems and counting for transverse subgroups
papers.abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. We study the joint distribution of partial Cartan projections and the two associated Cartan flags for Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups. Assuming local mixing of the associated Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan measure, we prove two local limit theorems and deduce counting asymptotics in Euclidean balls and tubes, together with equidistribution of the Cartan flags. These qualitative conclusions hold for $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, for which the local mixing hypothesis is satisfied. If the group is linearly $\theta$-regular near the direction of maximal growth, a polynomial error in local mixing gives polynomial errors in these results. Applying the quantitative local mixing theorem of Kim-Oh-Pan, we obtain local limit and counting theorems with polynomial error estimates for several classes of relatively Anosov representations of Fuchsian groups.

papers.title: Haar local mixing for transverse subgroups
papers.abstract: Transverse subgroups form a special class of discrete subgroups of connected semisimple real algebraic groups that includes all discrete subgroups of rank-one Lie groups, as well as Anosov and relatively Anosov subgroups. For torsion-free Zariski dense $\theta$-transverse subgroups, we establish Haar local mixing for the partial Weyl chamber action under a Bowen-Margulis-Sullivan (BMS) local mixing hypothesis. The proof is based on a transfer principle using the domains of discontinuity introduced by Delarue-Monclair-Sanders and extended to transverse subgroups by Guedes Bonthonneau-Lefeuvre-Weich. For $\theta$-Anosov subgroups, we verify the BMS hypothesis by adapting existing arguments and hence obtain Haar local mixing. As a consequence, we obtain asymptotics for the volume and distribution of long returns and recover the growth indicator from return volumes. Under linear $\theta$-regularity, the transfer also holds with polynomial error estimates. This condition is satisfied by subgroups of $\theta$-Anosov or relatively $\theta$-Anosov groups.

papers.title: Extensions of $q$-supercongruences arising from a quadratic summation of Gasper and Rahman
papers.abstract: In this paper, inspired by recent work of Guo and Zhao, and of Guo and Zudilin, we establish two parametric extensions of their $q$-supercongruences using Gasper and Rahman's quadratic summation, the Chinese remainder theorem, and the creative microscoping method. These extensions yield two one-parameter generalizations of the $q$-supercongruences considered by Guo and Zhao and by Guo and Zudilin.

papers.title: Sumsets modulo ideals: Baire category and descriptive complexity
papers.abstract: Given an ideal $\mathcal I$ on the nonnegative integers, we study the family $\Sigma(\mathcal I)$ of all sets for which every $\mathcal{I}$-small modification is not a nontrivial sumset $A+B$. We prove that $\Sigma(\mathcal I)$ is comeager whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is an Erd\H{o}s--Ulam ideal generated by a nonincreasing sequence of positive weights. This answers an open question for the ideal $\mathcal{Z}$ of asymptotic density zero sets in [Proc. Amer. Math. Soc. \textbf{151} (2023), 3681--3689]. We also show that $\Sigma(\mathcal I)$ is either empty or a dense $G_\delta$-complete set whenever $\mathcal{I}$ is an $F_\sigma$ ideal which is invariant under finite modifications. This implies that the family of nontrivial sumsets $A+B$ is $F_\sigma$-complete (hence, Borel). On the other hand, we construct a meager ideal $\mathcal{I}$ for which $\Sigma(\mathcal I)$ is neither meager nor comeager. Finally, we prove that $\Sigma(\mathcal Z)$ is coanalytic and not $F_{\sigma\delta}$.

papers.title: Asymptotics of a Gauss hypergeometric function related to moments of symmetric square L-functions I
papers.abstract: We prove an asymptotic formula for a special case of the Gauss hypergeometric function, which arises in the explicit formula for the second moment of Maass form symmetric-square $L$-functions.

papers.title: On a Problem of Kac concerning Anisotropic Lacunary Sums
papers.abstract: Given a sequence of integers $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ satisfying $\liminf_{k \rightarrow \infty}\frac{n_{k+1}}{n_k} \ge q > 1$, a scheme of real-valued weights $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$, and a function $f: \mathbb{T} = \mathbb{R}/\mathbb{Z} \to \mathbb{R}$, it is a classical problem to determine whether \[ S_N(x):=\frac{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N} f(n_k x)}{ \sqrt{\sum_{k=1}^N c_{k,N}^2}} \] converges to a normal distribution as $N \rightarrow \infty$. This question can be traced back to early works of Kac and Erd\H{o}s and has since then been investigated. It is well known that the asymptotic behavior of $S_N$ is determined not only by the analytic properties of $f$, but also by the arithmetic properties of the sequence $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$ and by the subtle interaction between the two. In this article, we identify conditions on $(n_k)_{k \in \mathbb{N}}$, $f$ and $(c_{k,N})_{k \leq N}$ that can be regarded as minimal for a central limit theorem to hold for $S_N$. This addresses a question raised by Mark Kac [Ann. of Math., 1946].

papers.title: Weil's quadratic form via the screw function
papers.abstract: We establish a unified operator-theoretic framework for understanding the results on the Weil quadratic form obtained by Yoshida (1992), Bombieri (2001, 2003), Connes--Consani (2023), and Connes--Consani--Moscovici (2025+) from the perspective of the screw function introduced in Suzuki (2023). An advantage of the approach via the screw function is that it provides a method to study the Weil quadratic form, which is originally defined in terms of distributions, by means of continuous functions and brings the theory of de Branges spaces into the analysis of the Weil quadratic form via the Fourier transform. Based on this framework, we formulate a conjecture stating that a self-adjoint operator whose eigenvalues are the imaginary parts of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function can be obtained as the limit, as $a \to \infty$, of self-adjoint operators arising from nonlocal realizations of the first-order differential operator on the finite interval $[-a,a]$. All these results are obtained without assuming the Riemann Hypothesis. This conjecture may be compared with the limit formula for the Riemann zeta function expressed in terms of zeta-regularized products proposed by Connes, Consani, and Moscovici, and it sheds new light on the spectral-theoretic interpretation of the nontrivial zeros of the Riemann zeta function.

papers.title: Spectral and Isoperimetric Bounds on Flat Tori
papers.abstract: We record several elementary relations between spectral and isoperimetric parameters of a flat torus $\mathbb{T}_\Lambda = \mathbb{R}^n/\Lambda$ and the covariance structure of a fundamental domain $K$ for the lattice $\Lambda \subset \mathbb{R}^n$. For every measurable fundamental domain $K$ and nonzero vector $\xi$ in the dual lattice $\Lambda^*$, we observe the sharp directional variance estimate \[ \left\langle \operatorname{Cov}_K \xi,\xi\right\rangle \geq \frac{1}{12}. \] This yields a lower bound on the torus spectral gap $\lambda_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda)$ (equivalently, the length of the shortest nonzero dual vector $\lambda_1(\Lambda^*)$) in terms of the maximal covariance of $K$: \[ \lambda_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda) = 4\pi^2 \lambda_1(\Lambda^*)^2 \geq \frac{\pi^2}{3\left\|\operatorname{Cov}_K\right\|_{\mathrm{op}}}. \] Analogous sharp results are obtained for the isoperimetric profile and the Cheeger constant $D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda)$ using an old argument of Hadwiger. In particular, when the Voronoi cell $K_\Lambda$ of a lattice with $\det \Lambda = 1$ is isotropic, the recent resolution of the Slicing Problem by Klartag and Lehec implies that \[ D_{\mathrm{Che}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda),\quad \lambda_{\mathrm{SG}}(\mathbb{T}_\Lambda),\quad \lambda_1(\Lambda^*) \geq c > 0, \] where $c > 0$ is a universal constant independent of dimension $n$; this may be thought of as a positive resolution of the Kannan--Lov\'asz--Simonovits conjecture for all flat tori. While there are lattices $\Lambda$ and corresponding Voronoi cells $K = K_\Lambda$ for which no dimension-independent converse inequality to the spectral-gap bound above can hold, we show that under a certain sectional tiling hypothesis, this inequality is in fact an equivalence (up to numerical constants).

papers.title: Landau's problems through ratios of $L$-functions
papers.abstract: Very recently, Lee announced a proof of the Twin Prime Conjecture assuming the Ratios Conjecture for the Riemann zeta function. We obtain conditional asymptotic formulas with power-saving errors for each of Landau's four prime problems. In the function field setting, using Sawin's estimates for factorization functions in squarefree progressions and a discriminant cohomology argument, we obtain unconditional Goldbach and prime-pair asymptotics over sufficiently large fixed odd fields, including prime fields. Similar results may be possible for other problems in analytic number theory.

papers.title: Irreducible Projective Polynomials
papers.abstract: Suppose $q=p^{s_1}$ and $\sigma=p^{s_2}$ for a prime $p$ and $s_1,s_2\in\mathbb{N}.$ In this paper, we characterize for which values of $p, d, s_1, s_2, \ell$ there exists an irreducible polynomials over $\mathbb{F}_q$ of the form \begin{align*} x^\frac{\sigma^d-1}{\ell}+\sum_{j=0}^{d-1}a_j x^\frac{\sigma^j-1}{\ell} \end{align*} for fixed $d,\ell\in\mathbb{N}$ where $\ell\mid (\sigma-1).$ In particular, we enumerate irreducible polynomials of this form.

papers.title: On p-adic modularity of abelian threefolds with imaginary multiplication and rational p-isogeny
papers.abstract: We prove $p$-adic modularity of a certain class of abelian threefolds over $\mathbf{Q}$ (with imaginary multiplication and rational $p$-isogeny), including the Jacobians of some genus 3 curves known as Picard curves. More precisely, we study a deformation problem for residual 3-dimensional totally reducible Galois pseudorepresentations over an imaginary quadratic field which are ordinary at primes over $p$ and conjugate self-dual. We show that under certain conditions the universal pseudodeformation ring in any weight (including the non-classical low weight corresponding to an abelian threefold) is isomorphic to a specialization of the ordinary Hida Hecke algebra on $U(2,1)$. The conditions that we assume are essentially class group conditions as well as weak regularity of the Hecke algebras in sufficiently high classical weights.

papers.title: The first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable
papers.abstract: We show that any ring of totally real abelian integers has a JR-number and therefore the first-order theory of every ring of totally real abelian integers is undecidable. It then follows that the first-order theory of the ring of integers of any abelian extension of $\Q$ is undecidable and that there is one formula without parameters defining $\Z$ in any such ring. The main arithmetic input is a recent paper of Bajpai, Das, Kedlaya, and Mello proving that the houses of cyclotomic integers form a well-ordered subset of $\R$.

papers.title: An ancient diophantine problem of Brahmagupta
papers.abstract: In the seventh century CE, Brahmagupta gave a parametric solution to the problem of finding two numbers $x$ and $y$ such that $x+y, x-y$ and $xy+1$ are all squares. We describe a method for generating infinitely many rational parametric solutions of the problem and another method for generating parametric solutions of the problem in terms of univariate polynomials with integer coefficients. The complete solution of the problem still remains elusive.

papers.title: Two-Sided large oscillations of the argument of the Riemann zeta function and its iterates
papers.abstract: Assuming the Riemann hypothesis, we establish lower bounds for large oscillations of the iterated argument functions \(S_n(t)\) of the Riemann zeta function. As a corollary, we prove that, for every fixed integer \(n \geq 0\), \[S_n(t)=\Omega_{\pm}\Big(\frac{(\log t)^{1/2}(\log_3 t)^{1/2}}{(\log_2 t)^{n+1/2}} \Big).\] For even \(n\), this recovers two results of Chirre and Mahatab in 2021. For odd \(n\), our result strengthens theirs by establishing the missing direction of oscillation with the same order of magnitude.
